maria: Hey — quick help. We're seeing a bunch of HTTP logs with X-Req-Id (eg req=abc123) but when I paste the req id into Jaeger/Tempo nothing shows. Where do people usually map request-id -> trace-id? Also need the dashboard/query to pull traces for a specific route. Thanks :pray:

jon: Short answer: logs need to contain the trace_id (or traceparent) for direct mapping. Two places to check first: (1) Kibana log field where we enrich logs (logstash/otel-collector pipeline) and (2) the traces backend (tempo/jaeger). If logs don't include trace_id we can't correlate.

maria: Ok — how do I see if logs are being enriched? I see an "otel" pipeline in infra but not sure what to search for.

jon: Run this Kibana query: `request_id: "abc123"` and then inspect the document fields. Look for either `trace.trace_id`, `trace_id`, or `log.attributes.trace_id`. Example filter bar: `request_id:"abc123" AND _exists_:trace.trace_id`. If that returns nothing, enrichment didn't happen.

sam: We recently rolled a change that only adds trace_id when the app forwards W3C traceparent header. If the client uses our X-Req-Id only, we intentionally don't reverse-lookup it to avoid perf hits. You can find the enrichment rule in the otel-collector config: `/infra/observability/collector/pipelines.yaml`.

lena: If you need a quick heuristic: take the request timestamp and span over the likely latency window (+- 2s) and search traces for the route and host. Use the traces search page, filter by `service:gateway` and `http.target:"/api/v1/…"` and narrow timeframe. That often surfaces candidate trace IDs.

maria: Any config snippet to make apps log the trace id? I can push a tiny change to the Go logger.

jon: Yep — in Go we use the otel SDK + logrus/text mapper. Quick example (add to request logging):

```
// extract trace id from ctx
span := trace.SpanFromContext(ctx)
if span.SpanContext().IsValid() {
  entry = entry.WithField("trace_id", span.SpanContext().TraceID().String())
}
log.Info(entry)
```

Also ensure the HTTP middleware injects the context properly (we use otelhttp).

maria: Great — and for services that only have X-Req-Id, can we backfill mappings?

sam: We have a small consumer that reads logs and emits mapping records into Redis for a short TTL — used for debugging. It was disabled last week for perf testing. Re-enable is possible but I'd rather add trace_id at source.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Observability pipeline deploy triggered by @sam — build #472 will touch collector config (only processors). ETA ~ 20m :gear:

jon: If you want to see the canonical dashboards:
- Kibana logs view: https://kibana.redwood-internal.com/app/logs (filter on request_id)
- Traces search: https://tempo.redwood-internal.com/search
- Per-route APM dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal.com/d/obs-routing/routes-overview

For sampling: if you see traces missing systematically it's often sampling. Our default is parentbased_traceidratio with 1% for background jobs. For services handling user requests we set 10% by default. Check `tracing.sampling.rate` in service config.

maria: Where do I change that if I want more for a short window?

jon: You can request a temporary increase by posting here and CC-ing @lena — ops can bump sampler for a rollout window. Or, alter local env var `TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE=0.2` for your staging box. For production, we need infra sign-off.

lena: I can do a short increase for debugging — ping me the service name + time window and I'll adjust. Also if you need a script to map request_id->trace_id from logs I can share one.

maria: Awesome — service is `gateway-prod-1` and I'd like a 1h bump to 30% starting in 10m. I'll also push the Go change with trace_id logging.

lena: Got it, updating sampler now. Will confirm when done. :white_check_mark:

jon: One more troubleshooting tip: if you're using the deploy agent (sidecar) it may rewrite headers. Check the ingress proxy config for `traceparent` passthrough. A missing header at the edge = no trace.

maria: Thanks everyone — I'll push the code change and re-check Kibana once the sampler is up. If I can't find the mapping I'll post a sample log output and timestamp.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Observability pipeline deploy succeeded (build #472) — collector processors updated.

lena: Sam, sampler bumped to 0.3 for gateway-prod-1 from 1917504600 to 1917508200.

maria: Confirmed I see `trace_id` in Kibana now for that request. Found the trace in Tempo using the id. Yay :tada:

jon: Nice! If anyone wants a tiny helper script I have a grep+tempo-lookup tool that does this mapping given request_id. I can drop in `#dev-tools` later.

maria: Please do. Closing this thread, thanks all :heart:
